## NeoOrigins v2.2.38

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Powers granted outside an origin now appear on the origin info screen, and mods can read and change a player's resources. Both editors now offer the conditions that control whether a whole power works, and the in-game creator can add lists of actions and conditions to power fields that accept them. The web editors can export for Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3, and exports for 26.1 now use the correct datapack format.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

- **Powers granted outside an origin appear on the origin info screen.** The screen previously listed only powers given by the player's origins, leaving granted powers out. An API-granted power now appears with the player's origin on the grant's layer, or with their main origin when the grant names no layer or a layer where they have no origin. Powers from `/power grant`, `grant_power` actions and global power sets appear in an **Other Powers** tab when no origin already lists them. Hidden powers stay hidden, and the tab only appears when it has powers to show. See [Granting powers at runtime](docs/JAVA_API.md#granting-powers-at-runtime).

- **Web exports for Minecraft 26.1 use the correct datapack format.** The origin and mob-origin editors wrote format 84, which is 26.1's resource-pack format, into their datapacks. They now write datapack format 101 and include the format range required by newer Minecraft versions. Importing an older format-84 editor export still selects 26.1, so exporting it again corrects its metadata.

- **Both editors offer the conditions that control a whole power.** The mod already read `power_condition` and `power_condition_mode`, but the editors did not offer them. Both fields now appear on every power: `ALLOW` enables the power while the condition passes, and `DENY`, the default for `power_condition`, disables it while the condition passes. Types without their own `condition` field also offer that field as an alias, including in the in-game creator; the alias defaults to `ALLOW`. Both the alias and `power_condition` take one condition object. A power type's own `condition` field keeps its existing meaning and format. See [Power types](docs/POWER_TYPES.md).

- **The in-game creator can add several actions or conditions to a power field.** Fields that accept either one action or condition or a list were offered as single-entry pickers in the creator, even though the web editor could already author lists. The creator now offers either form for those fields. The whole-power condition and its `condition` alias still take a single condition.

- **The web editor offers declared string choices as dropdowns.** A string field could declare a fixed set of choices, but those choices were left out of the editor's schema, so it offered a text box instead. Fields such as `effect_over_time.activation` now show their declared choices in a dropdown.

- **The web editor's built-in powers and origin templates use the current definitions.** The editor kept copies of these definitions that had fallen behind the mod's data, so starting from a template or copying a built-in power could bring back older settings. Both catalogs now match the shipped data.

- **The web editors can export for Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3.** The origin and mob-origin editors previously offered only 1.21.1 and 26.1. Both now include 26.2 and 26.3, with vanilla suggestions for each version. A 26.2 export uses datapack format 107 and a 26.3 export uses 121; importing either selects the matching target version.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.37

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> An `entity_model` power with a condition now changes the player's form as they play, so a werewolf can turn at night and change back at dawn. Mods can now run NeoOrigins actions in their own code, and the power grant and revoke events now tell a mod which type of power changed and how it was configured.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **An `entity_model` condition now changes the morph as you play (#141).** The player takes the form while the condition holds and changes back when it stops. Before, the condition was only checked when the player's powers were synced, such as on an origin change, so a werewolf could not turn at night. A morph change is sent at most every five ticks, and growing into a tight space still waits for room. See [Shapeshifting](docs/powers/visuals.md#shapeshifting).

### Mod Developer API

- **Mods can use NeoOrigins actions.** `parseAction` turns the JSON of any NeoOrigins entity action, such as `neoorigins:heal`, into a `Consumer<ServerPlayer>` a mod can run in its own code. `actionCodec` gives a mod's own power config an action field, so pack authors writing that power type in JSON can set actions in it. The field takes one action or a list that runs in order. An action that cannot be read does nothing and is logged with the power it belongs to. Actions that act on the triggering event, such as `damage_attacker` or `strip`, do nothing when a mod runs them outside a NeoOrigins event. See [Actions in your own code](docs/JAVA_API.md#actions-in-your-own-code).

- **Grant and revoke events carry the power.** `PowerGrantedEvent` and `PowerRevokedEvent` gave only the power's id, so a mod could not tell what type of power changed or read its settings. Both now give the full power with `getPower()`, its type with `getPowerType()` and `getPowerTypeId()`, and its config with `getConfig()`. A revoked power still carries the config it had. The events table in the API docs also now lists every path that fires them, including `/power grant`, the `grant_power` action and datapack reloads. See [Events](docs/JAVA_API.md#events-apievent).

### Installation
Download the JAR matching your Minecraft version and drop it into your `mods/` folder.
- `neoorigins-2.2.37+26.1.jar` — for MC 26.1, 26.1.1, and 26.1.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.37+26.2.jar` — for MC 26.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.37+26.3.jar` — for MC 26.3
- `neoorigins-2.2.37+1.21.1.jar` — for MC 1.21.1

### Origins Compatibility
Drop Origins mod content packs (`.jar`, `.zip`, or folder) into the `originpacks/` folder in your game directory.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.36

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Powers that other mods register in code can now be gated by a condition, pay toggle upkeep and carry their own resource bars, the same as powers written in a datapack. Mods can also read NeoOrigins conditions directly, either to check one in their own code or to let pack authors set one inside their own power types.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Mod Developer API

- **Code-registered powers take a condition gate.** A power added with `registerPower` had no way to be limited by a condition, so it could not do what `power_condition` does for a datapack power. `registerPower` now takes a `CodePowerOptions`, built with `CodePowerOptions.builder()`, whose `condition` accepts any `Predicate<ServerPlayer>`. By default the power only works while the condition is true; pass `ConditionMode.DENY` to block it while true instead. The gate covers ticking, activation, `onHit`, `onKill` and the power lookups on `NeoOriginsAPI`, exactly as `power_condition` does. The four-argument `registerPower` is unchanged. See [Condition gate, upkeep and toggle messages](docs/JAVA_API.md#condition-gate-upkeep-and-toggle-messages).

- **Code-registered toggles and resource bars work like datapack ones.** Toggle upkeep and `toggle_messages` were read only from a power's JSON, so a toggle registered in code could not charge hunger or a resource while on, and a resource bar registered in code had no id of its own. The same options now set `hungerCost`, `resourceCost`, `upkeepInterval`, `upkeepCondition` and `toggleMessages`. A resource or variable power stores its value under the id it is registered with, and `resource` conditions and `change_resource` can find it. These settings survive `/reload`, and a datapack power with the same id uses its own settings while it overrides the registered one. New `registerPowerFromJson` takes the config as the JSON a datapack power file would hold, and reads it the same way, `power_condition` included. See [Config from JSON](docs/JAVA_API.md#config-from-json).

- **Mods can use NeoOrigins conditions.** `parseCondition` turns the JSON of any NeoOrigins entity condition, such as `neoorigins:submerged_in`, into a `Predicate<ServerPlayer>` a mod can test in its own code or pass to a code-registered power. `conditionCodec` gives a mod's own power config a condition field, so pack authors writing that power type in JSON can set conditions in it. The field takes one condition or a list that must all pass. A condition that cannot be read evaluates false and is logged with the power it belongs to. See [Conditions in your own code](docs/JAVA_API.md#conditions-in-your-own-code).

### Installation
Download the JAR matching your Minecraft version and drop it into your `mods/` folder.
- `neoorigins-2.2.36+26.1.jar` — for MC 26.1, 26.1.1, and 26.1.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.36+26.2.jar` — for MC 26.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.36+26.3.jar` — for MC 26.3
- `neoorigins-2.2.36+1.21.1.jar` — for MC 1.21.1

### Origins Compatibility
Drop Origins mod content packs (`.jar`, `.zip`, or folder) into the `originpacks/` folder in your game directory.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.35

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Other mods can now build on NeoOrigins: they can back a resource bar with their own pool, read and change a player's origin, grant and revoke powers at runtime, and register powers in code. Resetting one layer with `/origin reset` no longer takes away the powers of the player's other layers, and an origin upgrade no longer hands out a unique origin that another player already holds. Editing a power and running `/reload` now updates the players who already hold it. Players can also hide the folded wings that powers such as the Elytrian's draw on their back.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **Origin upgrades respect unique origins.** On a layer where each origin can belong to only one player, an origin's `upgrades` entry still switched a player to its target origin when someone else already held it, leaving two players on a unique origin. While another player holds the target, the upgrade now does not happen and its announcement is not shown. `/origin set` is not affected: it gives the origin to the named player, who then holds the claim. See [Unique origin layers](docs/ADMIN_CONFIG.md#unique_origin_layers-one-player-per-origin).

### Configuration

- **Hide folded wings.** Wings that a power draws folded on the back while not gliding, such as the Elytrian's, can now be hidden with `hide_folded_wings` under the new `[wings]` section of `client.toml`. The wings still appear while gliding. The option only changes what you see: it applies to every player's wings on your screen and to no one else's. It is off by default, so nothing changes until you turn it on. See [Client config](docs/CLIENT_CONFIG.md#wings-power-granted-wings).

### Bug Fixes

- **Resetting one layer keeps the player's other powers.** `/origin reset <player> <layer>` cleared only the named layer, but it switched off the powers of every layer, so a player whose class was reset also lost their origin's powers, such as extra hearts, while keeping the origin itself. Powers granted with `grant_power` or `/power grant` were dropped too. It now removes only the named layer's powers.

- **Editing a power and reloading updates the players who hold it.** When a `/reload` changed what a power does, online players who already held it kept the old version: its old effects stayed and the new ones never applied until they relogged, and taking the power away afterwards could leave an old effect behind, such as extra hearts. After a reload, each held power whose definition changed is now removed in its old form and applied in its new form, once. A reload that changes nothing leaves powers, resource bars and toggles exactly as they were. See [Hot-reload](docs/guides/testing.md#hot-reload).

### Mod Developer API

- **Other mods can back a resource bar (#140).** A `neoorigins:resource` bar's `backing` could only be `irons_spellbooks:mana`. A mod can now register its own pool with `NeoOriginsAPI.registerResourceBacking`, and a pack names it the same way, for example `"backing": "mymod:stamina"`. The bar reads that pool, sends every change to it and scales to its live maximum. A backing that does not take an absolute value ignores `set_resource` with one warning, a backing whose mod is missing leaves the bar empty, and a `backing` id that no installed mod registers keeps the bar in NeoOrigins' own store, with a warning. Iron's Spells mana works as before. See [Resource backings](docs/JAVA_API.md#resource-backings).

## NeoOrigins v2.2.34

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Origin upgrades now happen for advancements written without a `display` block, and their announcements go to the whole server and name the player who upgraded. A new `gameplay.toml` option chooses who sees them.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **Origin upgrade announcements reach the whole server.** When an origin's `upgrades` entry switches a player to a new origin, its `announcement` used to be shown only to that player. It is now broadcast to everyone online. To keep the old behaviour, set `mode = "PLAYER"` under the new `[upgrade_announcements]` section of `gameplay.toml`, or `"OFF"` to hide announcements entirely. An existing config gains the section, set to `SERVER`, the next time the game starts. See [Gameplay config](docs/GAMEPLAY_CONFIG.md#upgrade_announcements-origin-upgrade-announcements).

### Bug Fixes

- **`%s` in an upgrade announcement names the player.** The web editor's own example, `%s has ascended to Archmage!`, expects the player's name in place of `%s`, but no name was ever passed in, so the line showed a literal `%s`. The upgraded player's name now fills it, whether the announcement is plain text or a translation key. Announcements without a `%s` read as before. See [Pack format](docs/PACK_FORMAT.md).

- **Origin upgrades happen for advancements without a `display` block.** An upgrade waited for the game's advancement-earned event, which NeoForge sends only for advancements that have a `display` block, so an upgrade tied to a hidden trigger advancement written without one never happened. Upgrades now take effect on the criterion that completes the advancement, with or without a display, and a further criterion granted to an advancement that is already complete does not set them off again.

### Installation
Download the JAR matching your Minecraft version and drop it into your `mods/` folder.
- `neoorigins-2.2.34+26.1.jar` — for MC 26.1, 26.1.1, and 26.1.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.34+26.2.jar` — for MC 26.2
- `neoorigins-2.2.34+26.3.jar` — for MC 26.3
- `neoorigins-2.2.34+1.21.1.jar` — for MC 1.21.1

### Origins Compatibility
Drop Origins mod content packs (`.jar`, `.zip`, or folder) into the `originpacks/` folder in your game directory.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.33

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Three fixes for phasing through walls: Spectral Form no longer slips out through the world border, portals work while phasing, and limited sight follows the player's eyes in both F5 views. The four summoning abilities cost half the hunger they had been taking, and fifteen ability descriptions stop naming a resource cost that was never charged. For pack authors, seven more active power types now charge `resource_cost`, and `neoorigins:toggle` can pay its own hunger or resource upkeep without a separate charging power. Older origin packs have more of their 1.20 data and commands rewritten into the current format as they are read, including the loot data that stopped a 26.3 server from starting, and on 26.3 an origin pack file that still cannot be read is now skipped with a warning instead.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Bug Fixes

- **Spectral Form no longer leaves the world border.** Phasing switches off the collision the world border is built out of, so a phasing player walked straight through the border and lost their flight through blocks on the far side. A phasing player now stops at the border's face with no rubber-banding, and one who is already outside is put back inside, half a block in from the face. Phase Walk, Phase Step and Void Phase also refuse to land outside: their scan reaches far enough ahead to cross the border from just inside, and teleporting bypasses movement collision checks. The classic Phantom's Phasing and the Evolved and Apex tiers of Spectral Form are covered the same way.

- **Portals work while phasing.** A player phasing with Spectral Form or the classic Phantom's Phasing who stood in a nether portal never travelled. The same switched-off collision meant the game never offered the portal its chance to claim them. End portals and end gateways were in the same position, and all three work now. Nothing else a phasing player passes through has changed: cactus, fire, sweet berries, cobwebs and powder snow still have no effect while incorporeal.

- **Summoning costs half the hunger it was taking.** Abyssal Command, Call of the Deep, Raise Skeleton Archer and Raise Wither Skeleton each charged their hunger cost twice, so every summon took 8 food points instead of 4. Each now charges once, however many minions it spawns. Taming was never affected.

- **Fifteen abilities no longer name a cost they never charged.** v2.2.32 corrected the resource costs quoted in ability descriptions to match what the bar actually loses. For fifteen of them the bar lost nothing at all, because the power types behind them never read `resource_cost`: Void Step, Ender Warp, Warp Step, Shadow Step, Phase Walk, Void Phase, both Shadow Orbs, the Earth Mage's Ground Slam, Tidal Wave, Stone Light and the four summoning abilities have spent nothing from their resource bars in every release. Their descriptions no longer mention a resource cost, in all twelve languages. Hunger costs are unchanged, apart from the summoning fix above.

- **Phasing fog follows the player's eyes, not the camera.** With `obscured_vision` enabled, moving the F5 camera against a wall could darken the whole view while the player was standing in open air. The solid-block check was using the detached camera's position, so even a camera brushing a wall post could trigger it. It now uses the player's eye position in first person and both F5 views. A player whose eyes are inside a wall stays fogged even if the camera is outside, so switching views does not bypass the fog. See [Limited sight while phasing](docs/powers/movement.md#neooriginswraith_phase).

### Pack Author Features

## NeoOrigins v2.2.32

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> Toggle powers can now cost something to keep running. Any toggle, from flight to stealth, can now be configured to consume hunger or a resource while it is on and to switch off when the player can no longer pay, and `effect_over_time` charges its upkeep in every mode. Riding the Sword is the first built-in power to use it: flying on the blade costs 1 hunger point every 3 seconds. A new `personal_dimension` power type, marked \<Experimental\>, gives a player a room of their own in a new dimension, kept between visits, and pack authors get text colours and outlines for resource bars, a way to silence toggle messages, a running cost for the extra inventory, and fog for players phasing through walls. Lucky Trader now does what its name says and makes trades cheaper.
>
> Most of the rest of this release makes the classes do what their descriptions say. More than sixty previously ineffective settings in `power_overrides.toml` now change the values they name, Charisma and Scavenging no longer hand out duplicates, Seal's Grace and the classic Mining Expert work, and every class description now states the real numbers. The 26.x builds pick up the 1.21.1 fixes they were missing, and the documentation is reorganised around a new start page, with a page listing every class power and its exact numbers.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **Riding the Sword costs hunger while you fly.** The Sword Immortal's flight now takes 1 hunger point every 3 seconds, charged only while you are actually in the air, so standing or walking with the art switched on is free. Saturation is spent first, as with sprinting. When you can no longer pay, the art switches off and you drop, and Immortal Body still means the fall does no damage. Server owners can change the cost with `hunger_cost` and `upkeep_interval` under `[power_overrides.jianxian_riding_sword]`.

- **Lucky Trader makes trades cheaper.** The Merchant's Lucky Trader gave +1 Luck and nothing else, and Luck has no effect on trading: in vanilla it only changes fishing catches. It keeps the +1 Luck and now also lowers the first cost of every villager and wandering trader offer by about 10%, rounded in your favour, so anything costing 2 or more is at least 1 cheaper (5 emeralds becomes 4, 20 becomes 18). The discount applies when the trade screen opens and stacks with Hero of the Village and villager reputation.

- **Timber! needs an axe.** The Lumberjack felled a whole tree whatever broke the log, including a bare hand or a pickaxe. It now fells only when the log is broken with an axe, or with an empty hand while Axe Hands is active.

- **Beacon Regeneration needs a working beacon.** The Paladin regenerated next to any beacon block, including one with no pyramid or a blocked beam. It now needs a beacon that would give its own effects.

- **Two class powers have new names.** The Warrior's +2 armor power is now Battle-Hardened, so the class no longer shows two powers called Battle Stance. The classic Rogue's Stealth description card is now Vanish, for the same reason.

- **Classic mode turns evolution off.** Classic mode only turned evolution off in practice: the classic origins and classes have no tiers, but kills were still counted and evolution prompts still appeared that granted nothing. While `classic_mode` is on, evolution is now fully off whatever `gameplay.toml` says, for datapack and `originpacks/` origins too: kills are not counted, no prompt appears, and the info screen hides the Evolution Path. A tier a player already reached is kept and applies again if classic mode is switched off.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.31

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, **26.3**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> The headline is classic mode: a new `content.toml` switch that offers only the original Origins mod's ten origins and the fourteen Origins: Classes classes, each with a power set modelled on the original mod. Turn it on before the world is created if you can: players who already have an origin or class hidden by classic mode keep it until they reset it.
>
> Rebuilding those sets added four power types for pack authors, and Origins packs that use Blazeborn's snowball weakness, the Merling's conduit power, the Arachnid's webs or `entity_glow` now behave as they do in Origins. Two reports late in testing turned into a further batch of compatibility fixes: an imported resource bar keeps the value you earned rather than resetting on every world join, and an attribute can now follow a resource, as Apoli packs expect of it. Three well-known Origins powers that loaded and did nothing now work, and a power handler registered from a KubeJS `startup_scripts/` file remains registered when a world loads.
>
> This release also brings NeoOrigins to Minecraft 26.3. A client running Punchy, or any mod that checks item use animations often, no longer loses about a third of every frame to NeoOrigins when a pack loads Origins-format powers (#136), and flight powers such as Riding the Sword can no longer be switched off by mods that reset player flight every tick, such as Create Buzzy Beez. Each resource bar can now be resized in the origin editor, and a new `dynamic` flag stacks cooldown and timer bars above the permanent ones.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.3 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **Classic mode.** A new `classic_mode` option in `content.toml`, off by default, offers only the original Origins mod's ten origins and the fourteen Origins: Classes classes, each with a power set modelled on the original mod. The origins are Human, Merling, Avian, Blazeborn, Elytrian, Enderian, Arachnid, Shulk, Phantom and Feline. The classes are Archer, Beastmaster, Blacksmith, Cleric, Cook, Explorer, Farmer, Lumberjack, Merchant, Miner, Nitwit, Rancher, Rogue and Warrior. Farmer and Rancher are new, and only appear in classic mode. While it is on, every other built-in origin and class is hidden whatever its toggle says, and so are the three Dragon Survival dragons. A classic origin or class switched off by its own toggle stays hidden, and origins from datapacks or `originpacks/` are still offered. Switching it while the server runs applies at once: online players holding a classic origin swap power sets, powers both versions share keep their state, and every client's picker is resent. See [CONTENT_CONFIG.md](docs/CONTENT_CONFIG.md#classic-mode).

- **Turn classic mode on before the world is created if you can.** A player who already holds a built-in origin or class that classic mode hides keeps it, powers and all, until it is reset with an Orb of Origin or an Orb of Class, or by an admin running `/neoorigins reset <player>`. Affected players receive a chat message explaining this and how to reset their origin or class, every time they join and when the mode is switched on while they are online. The server also logs a warning when a world that already has player data starts with classic mode on, or has it switched on while running.

- **Classic mode turns evolution off in practice.** None of the classic origins has evolution tiers, and every other built-in is hidden while the mode is on, so none of the selectable built-in origins evolves. Kill counts stop mattering until the mode goes off again. Datapack and `originpacks/` origins keep whatever tiers they declare.

- **`/neoorigins list` shows what classic mode hides.** Hidden entries are marked `[disabled]`, and the header says `(classic mode)` while it is on.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.30

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> A small release for the resource bar HUD and for pack commands. Resource bars now stack in a fixed, predictable order instead of one that followed an internal hash, with no empty slot left behind a bar that is hidden or dragged to its own position, and no bar's text printed over another bar's. The bars also get a new look: the built-in ones now draw in a framed style with value ticks, most with a scrolling fill themed to their origin, and packs can use the same eight styles, tint the plain one any colour, and run a bar from one colour into another. For pack authors, a command that does not parse is now written to the log along with the power that ran it, where before it failed in complete silence, and a valid `execute ... run` chain is no longer mistaken for a broken command by the legacy translation layer.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

### Changes

- **Resource bars stack in resource id order, lowest id nearest the hotbar.** The client kept its bars in a hash map, so the vertical order of the stack followed the resource keys' string hashes: stable for a given set of bars, but nothing a pack could predict, describe to a player, or control, and adding one resource dropped its bar wherever its hash happened to fall. A full sync now stores the bars sorted by resource key, which is the power id, and value updates leave each bar where it is. This rearranges existing stacks: any two or more bars sitting at their default positions, whose hash order differed from their id order, will have moved. Bars given a saved position in the HUD editor are unaffected. [POWER_TYPES.md](docs/POWER_TYPES.md) describes the order and which bars take a slot.

- **The built-in resource bars use the new bar styles.** Every origin that shows a resource bar now draws it in a framed style with value ticks: a scrolling themed fill where the origin has a clear element, such as fire for the Blazeling, water for the Kraken, void for the Enderian and sculk for the Warden, and otherwise the plain grey fill tinted to the bar's existing colour. The Frostborn bar is the one exception: it was orange and is now an ice gradient, blue at the empty end shading to frost white at the full end. Only the look changed: no resource values, regeneration or costs moved.

### Bug Fixes

- **A hidden or repositioned resource bar no longer leaves a gap in the stack.** The HUD advanced its stacking counter for every bar it knew about, whether or not that bar was drawn in the stack, so a bar hidden by hide when full, or one moved to a saved position in the HUD editor, still reserved its slot and the bars above it did not close up. The draw decision is now made for every bar first, and slots are handed only to the bars that will actually draw at a default position. The HUD editor assigns its slots the same way, so the gap that used to sit behind a dragged bar there is gone as well.

- **Stacked resource bars no longer print their text over each other.** Every bar draws its name above it and its value below it, but the stack climbed a fixed sixteen pixels per bar, which is less than a bar and its two lines of text need. Each bar's value landed on the name of the bar below it, so in a stack of several bars everything between the top name and the bottom value was an unreadable pile. Each slot is now as tall as what its bar actually draws: the bar, the name line, the value line and a small gap, which puts the built-in framed bars 29 pixels apart. A bar whose `label` is empty draws no name line and takes a shorter slot, though never shorter than the old sixteen. The HUD editor measures its bars the same way, so its default stack uses the same spacing as the HUD. [POWER_TYPES.md](docs/POWER_TYPES.md) describes the slot sizes.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.29

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> A fixes release, mostly for the two origin editors, which could quietly lose data on save. Saving a power in the in-game creator deleted any detail its form could not display, loading a template and saving it dropped the origin's evolution tiers and custom spawn, one creator save could overwrite another origin's power files, and the web editor started new origins in the `neoorigins` namespace, where a name matching a shipped origin replaced it for the whole server. Outside the editors, an `area_of_effect` with a block action and no radius no longer runs that action across seventeen thousand blocks, one invalid origin id no longer empties an entire origin layer, and origin spawn searches start from the world spawn instead of the wrong end of the map. On 1.21.1 other players are drawn in their own model colour rather than yours.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

- **An `area_of_effect` with a block action no longer runs it across seventeen thousand blocks.** The block sweep borrowed the entity sweep's default radius of sixteen, so a `block_action` with no radius written ran at every block within sixteen of the centre: 17,077 positions per activation, and with `explode` as the block action the server stalled. The block sweep now defaults to two blocks, thirty-three positions, while the entity sweep keeps its sixteen, and a radius you do write is honoured as before up to the existing cap of sixteen. Separately, `explode` is limited to four per player per tick. They all go off at the player rather than the swept block, and hurt immunity after the first absorbs most of what the rest would deal, so the extras bought lag and nothing else. [ACTIONS.md](docs/ACTIONS.md) records both defaults and the cap.
- **One invalid origin id no longer empties a whole origin layer.** An id the game cannot parse, such as a web export named `Wizard` or `wizard ` with a trailing space, threw while its layer was being read, and the loader's answer was to discard the entire layer. Since addon and exported packs add to the built-in `neoorigins:origin` and `neoorigins:class` layers, one bad id emptied the picker of every origin, or every class, for everyone on the server, with nothing on screen to say why. The bad entry is now skipped with a warning naming it, and the rest of the layer loads.
- **Origin spawn searches start from the world spawn, scaled into the searched dimension the way a portal scales it.** On 1.21.1 only the Nether was wrong: the search read the Overworld's spawn point without dividing by eight, so a world spawn at 8000, 0 sent a new Blazeling to Nether 8000, 0, sixty-four thousand blocks out in Overworld terms. On 26.1 and 26.2 every search started from 0, 0 in whatever dimension it searched, so all nine built-in origins with a spawn location ignored a moved world spawn. All three versions now start from the world spawn converted into the searched dimension, so an Overworld spawn at 8000, 0 centres a Nether search on 1000, 0, with the height kept inside build limits and the position inside the world border. [PACK_FORMAT.md](docs/PACK_FORMAT.md) covers `spawn_location` itself.
- **Every player is drawn in their own model colour instead of yours (1.21.1).** `model_color` tints were read from your own powers for every player on screen, so everyone around you wore your colour and nobody ever saw theirs. Each player's tint now comes from that player's own synced powers, clears when their effect ends, and is dropped when they log out or leave range. Minecraft 26.1 and 26.2 draw no model colours, since the 26.1 rendering rework removed the call the tint depends on.

## NeoOrigins v2.2.28

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2**, **26.2**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

> A large fixes release, and one of them is a crash. On 1.21.1, installing a resource pack built from our own theme template could kill the client at boot, or stop a server loading its datapacks, and the template shipped in a state that triggered both. All three are fixed, and a theme whose panel texture is missing now falls back to the parchment panel instead of stretching the missing-texture checkerboard across the origin screen. Elytrian now wears its wings folded on its back instead of showing them only mid-glide (#130), through a new third setting on `render_elytra` that every editor offers as a dropdown, and on 26.1 and 26.2 a chestplate no longer hides power-granted wings. The Rogue's one Class Skill key now goes to Step Assist, so the switch the Rogue gained in 2.2.26 can finally be pressed, and sneaking stops a step-assisted player at a ledge again (#134). The slime's bounce keeps a running player's speed, and a jump or a short drop no longer sets it off (#133). Resource bars stay on screen until you spend the resource for the first time (#105), come back by themselves after a `/reload`, and one player losing a resource power no longer takes every other holder's bar with it. The wraith's client and server now read its blocked-block list the same way (#109). Several fixes change what players feel without any visible change to the origin: power modifiers stopped adding another copy of themselves on every death and relog, the Sporeling's Fungal Contact heals only on mushroom blocks and mycelium as its description says, the Slime's tier-2 Sticky Aura slows things for the first time, and two powers that could never fire now do, one of them a Piglin downside. The Lumberjack pays its bonus planks for every wood rather than only oak. The three Dragon Survival origins can be picked at all now, and a random roll will not turn you into one. The in-game creator stops offering an operation that its own maths reads as an addition, the web editor's block view stops quietly rewriting the powers it loads, and both editors gained fields they could never author. Fish counts as meat for the Origins-compatible carnivore and vegetarian diets. Every config option and every entity has an English name, where the config screen had been drawing raw keys for a couple of hundred of them. The One Probe works on 26.1 and 26.2 for the first time, FTB Quests tag-marker rewards grant again on 26.1, and KubeJS scripts can read a player's resource values on 1.21.1 and 26.1.
>
> **Supports:** Minecraft 26.1.x (Java 25) · Minecraft 26.2 (Java 25) · Minecraft 1.21.1 (Java 21)

- **Elytrian keeps its wings on its back (#130).** Wings drawn by a flight power appeared only while the player was gliding, so an origin whose whole body plan is wings looked wingless the moment it landed. Elytrian now shows them folded on its back whenever its flight power is active, and spreads them in a glide as it always has. The other flying origins are unchanged: Phantom, Hiveling and Draconic still show wings only while gliding, and Windwalker still shows none. The setting behind this is described under Pack Author Features.

- **The Rogue's Class Skill key goes to Step Assist.** A class gets exactly one Class Skill key, and it goes to the first power in the class that can be activated. The Rogue listed Stealth ahead of the Step Assist switch it gained in 2.2.26, so Stealth took the key and Step Assist could not be switched at all. Step Assist is now first. Stealth is still granted and works as before (sneak for ten seconds and you turn invisible), but it no longer has a key, so it stays on.

## NeoOrigins v1.14.2

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2** and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

v1.14.2 — Turkish-locale hotfix

Patch release fixing a client-side crash for players running the JVM in
Turkish locale (tr_TR).

All five enum codecs in NeoOrigins (Impact, Condition, Action, ActiveWhen,
ActionType) called `String.toUpperCase()` / `toLowerCase()` without
specifying a locale. In Turkish locale, `"medium".toUpperCase()` returns
`"MEDİUM"` (with a dotted capital I) instead of `"MEDIUM"`, which fails
`Impact.valueOf()` and crashes the client on the `sync_origin_registry`
payload every time they try to join a server.

Symptom reported in the wild: `Failed to decode packet
'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload'` on login, only for one specific
player in a party (the one whose JVM defaults to tr_TR). The misleading
Sable crash banner — "Please make sure this issue is not caused by Sable"
— hides the real root cause, which is NeoOrigins.

Every affected codec now passes `Locale.ROOT` explicitly:

```java
s -> Impact.valueOf(s.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT))
```

Four power classes + the Impact enum updated. No schema changes; packs
that worked on v1.14.1 continue to work without edits.

Any player whose JVM defaults to a locale where letter-case conversion
produces non-ASCII characters — Turkish (tr_TR), Azerbaijani (az_AZ), and
a handful of others. Latin-locale users were never affected.

Thanks to RadexKonera for the detailed crash report.

### Installation
Download the JAR matching your Minecraft version and drop it into your `mods/` folder.
- `neoorigins-1.14.2+26.1.jar` — for MC 26.1, 26.1.1, and 26.1.2
- `neoorigins-1.14.2+1.21.1.jar` — for MC 1.21.1

### Origins Compatibility
Drop Origins mod content packs (`.jar`, `.zip`, or folder) into the `originpacks/` folder in your game directory.

## NeoOrigins v1.14.1

Built for **Minecraft 26.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.1.2** and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

v1.14.1 — minion friendly-fire fix + pet-leash tuning

Patch release addressing three tester-reported regressions affecting summoned
and tamed mobs. Drop-in replacement for v1.14.0 — no schema changes, no new
power types, no pack migrations needed.

- **Minions no longer attack their summoner.** Summons via `neoorigins:summon_minion`
  (Abyssal guardians, Necromancer skeletons, etc.) were spawning with their
  default vanilla AI — which still targets the nearest player, including the
  one who summoned them. They now receive the same owner-aware AI rewrite as
  tamed mobs, and event-level chokepoints catch anything that still slips
  through.

- **Tamed mobs forgive accidental owner hits.** `HurtByTargetGoal` was naive —
  any damage source flipped the pet hostile against the owner, including
  collision nudges, AoE splashback, and thorns reflection. A new
  `OwnerAwareHurtByTargetGoal` subclass clears `lastHurtByMob` when the owner
  is the source and declines to target.

- **Pet leash loosened.** `FollowOwnerGoal` teleport distance raised from 10 →
  24 blocks, follow-start from 3 → 8. Pets now have real room to engage
  enemies without snapping back to the owner every few steps.

- **Primed creepers defuse before leash-teleport.** A tamed creeper that began
  its swell at a distant target would detonate on top of the owner the
  instant the leash teleported it back. Creeper `swellDir` is now reset to
  -1 before the teleport call.

### Installation
Download the JAR matching your Minecraft version and drop it into your `mods/` folder.
- `neoorigins-1.14.1+26.1.jar` — for MC 26.1, 26.1.1, and 26.1.2
- `neoorigins-1.14.1+1.21.1.jar` — for MC 1.21.1

### Origins Compatibility

## NeoOrigins v1.2.1

Built for **Minecraft 26.1**, **26.1.1**, and **1.21.1** with **NeoForge**.

### Escalating XP Cost
Each time you use the Orb of Origin, the XP cost increases by 5 levels. Your first use is free, the second costs 5 levels, the third costs 10, and so on. Creative mode bypasses the cost.

### MC 1.21.1 Backport
NeoOrigins v1.2.0 content is now available for Minecraft 1.21.1 (NeoForge 21.1.224). All 35 origins, 17 classes, config system, and minion summoning are included.
